CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Semarang City.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of Almighty God and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
6. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
7. Protection of Women is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
9. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society.
10. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development.

Letter e

Letter f

Letter h

CHAPTER VI

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION STRATEGY

Article 23

1. Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data based on laws and regulations.
2. Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be implemented with working groups and/or integrated services established by Mayor's Decree.
3. Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection.

CHAPTER VIII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 29

1. The Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection functions as the leading sector in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
2. Further provisions regarding the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

PARTICIPATION

Article 30

1. The community, community groups/community organizations, business sector, academics, and/or other professional groups may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.

a. cooperation;

Article 25

1. Formulation of program and activity planning policies as referred to in Article 24 letter a, shall be implemented through:
a. mapping, collecting, processing and presenting data;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity planning preparation with relevant Regional Apparatus; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. Formulation of program and activity planning policies shall be implemented based on minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
3. Formulation of program and activity planning policies for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in the community. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.
